title: Resolved: Graph fails to render on Windows due to silent converters.ts script failure
body:
## Describe the bug
On a standard Windows environment using Anaconda for Python management, the application successfully completes the long-running GraphRAG indexing process and creates valid .parquet files in the output directory. However, the subsequent, automatic step to convert these .parquet files into .json files for the frontend visualization fails silently. This results in the UI always showing a "Failed to fetch relationships.json: Not Found" error, preventing any graph from being displayed.

The core issue appears to be that the Python script responsible for the Parquet-to-JSON conversion is not executing correctly, even after hardcoding the absolute path to the correct Python executable.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

Environment Setup:
Use a Windows 10 or Windows 11 machine.
Install Anaconda or Miniconda.
Install Git for Windows (which includes Git Bash).
Install Node.js (e.g., v22+).

Project Setup:
Create a specific Conda environment with a compatible Python version: conda create --name graphrag_env python=3.11
Initialize Conda for use with the Git Bash shell: conda init bash
Open a new Git Bash terminal.
Activate the environment: conda activate graphrag_env
Clone the repository: git clone https://github.com/ChristopherLyon/graphrag-workbench.git
Navigate into the project: cd graphrag-workbench

Install all dependencies:
pip install graphrag pandas pyarrow
npm install
Create a .env file from the example and add a valid OpenAI API key.

Required Code Modifications:
In app/api/corpus/index/stream/route.ts, modify the cmd variable (in both places it appears) to use the absolute path to the Conda environment's Python executable to fix a "command not found" error during indexing.
Change: const cmd = \graphrag index --config ${configFile}``
To: const cmd = \"C:/Users/YOUR_USER/anaconda3/envs/graphrag_env/python.exe" -m graphrag index --config ${configFile}``
In lib/server/converters.ts, modify the py variable inside the readParquetViaPython function to use the same absolute path, in an attempt to fix the silent conversion failure.
Change: const py = process.env.PYTHON || 'python3'
To: const py = "C:/Users/YOUR_USER/anaconda3/envs/graphrag_env/python.exe"
Execution:
Start the application from Git Bash (with the Conda env active): npm run dev
Open http://localhost:3000 in a browser.
Upload a PDF document known to contain entities and relationships.
Click "Run Index".


## Expected behavior
After the long indexing process completes (the log shows GET /api/corpus/index/stream 200 after several minutes), the .parquet files in the output/ directory should be successfully converted to their .json counterparts (e.g., relationships.json). The web UI should then fetch these JSON files and render the interactive knowledge graph.


## Actual behavior
The indexing process runs for several minutes and completes successfully. Non-empty .parquet files (e.g., relationships.parquet) are correctly created in the output/ directory.
However, the conversion to .json fails silently. The output/ directory never contains any .json files.
The web UI immediately shows a console error: Failed to fetch relationships.json: Not Found, and the visualization area remains blank. This is confirmed by the terminal log showing GET /api/data/relationships.json 404.


## Environment
OS: Windows 11
Python version: 3.11.9 (via Anaconda)
Node version: v22.18.0

## Additional context
I have exhaustively troubleshooted this issue, using mostly Gemini Pro 2.5 as an assistant., and tried with multiple PDFs with various lengths. The problem is not with the main GraphRAG indexing, but specifically with the readParquetViaPython fallback function in lib/server/converters.ts.

Despite hardcoding the absolute path to the correct Python executable (which has pyarrow and pandas installed), the execFileP process seems to fail without bubbling up an error to the Next.js console. The application behaves as if the conversion was never attempted or failed silently, leading directly to the 404 errors in the UI. This suggests a potential issue with how child_process.execFile is interacting with the Conda Python executable on Windows. So, I'm suspecting that this may be something about my system. When I have the time, I will return to this issue and try to solve it again as I may be missing something at the moment.

title: Use Local HuggingFace Models Instead of OpenAI
body:
Hi, thanks for the great project!

I’d like to run GraphRAG Workbench fully locally using HuggingFace models (e.g. google/gemma-3-270m for chat and sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 for embeddings) instead of OpenAI.

I updated settings.yaml and .env to point to HuggingFace, but still getting used by OpenAI's API

## Additional context

Can you clarify if local-only HuggingFace models are supported, and what the correct config is to avoid OpenAI API key requirements?

Thanks!

title: Import pre-computed graphrag output
body: It would be nice to have the possibility to import the precomputed "output" directory from a graphrag project. At the moment you need to upload pdf and compute the whole thing from scratch.
